content.text: {"headline":"Recommend P0: no action. The forecast already clears the 80% target at no cost and with no policy issues.","why":"The spike is caused by the P1 UPI switch incident (INC-20261006-6998, opened 10:31). At 10:30, 213 payments calls arrived against 111.9 forecast. Service level dropped to 4.7% and 59 calls were abandoned. Over the last four intervals, upi_payment_failed calls ran at 2.56x normal (183 vs 71.4 expected). Staffing is at plan (42 of 43), handle time is below forecast, and there are no campaigns or unusual absences, so this is an outage, not a staffing problem. With no action, the forecast is 85.1% overall (payments 83.3%, general 87.7%) with 3.7% abandons. That is above the 80% target, costs ₹0 and breaks no policy.","trade_offs":["P2 (₹468) gives only slightly better results: 85.8% overall, payments 84.6%, abandons 3.3%. However, moving 3 agents would drop general to 59% during 11:30-13:00, below the 70% floor (MOV-03).","P1 costs nothing but predicts a lower result than doing nothing (83.8%). It breaches MOV-03 (general at 61%) and BRK-04 (5 agents with more than one break delayed).","P3 (₹8,388, 88.8%) and P4 (₹9,000, 89.6%) cut abandons to about 2.5%. They cost far more and both breach BRK-04. That spend buys margin the target does not require."],"watch":"P0's payments forecast of 83.3% leaves little margin, and it assumes the outage-driven demand eases. Track payments service level and arrivals each interval, along with the incident status. If the UPI incident runs longer or payments falls toward 80%, reconsider P2. Fix its general-queue floor breach first, for example by deflection alone with no agent move. P3 is the fallback if a bigger response is needed."}
